I said it in a post about Scotland's ban on GM crops and I'll say it again, I see nothing wrong with a democracy deciding to banning GM crops.

Before the pro-GMO people start bashing and labeling Germany and Scotland as stupid or anti-science, all explain some of the reason why it may be in their countries interest to uphold bans on GM crops

1. Enviromental factors: GM crops tend to use more pesticides (herbicides) which can effect waterways and native fish, insects, reptiles, soil microbiology, invertebrates, and amphibians.

2. While the technology of Genetic Modification is likely safe, how the technology is used may not be. Example engineering a plant to withstand a herbicide that has a conflicting long term safety record. (Glyphosate herbicide are relatively safe in terms of acute toxicity, but are extremely questionable in long-term toxicity) If GM technology was instead used to improve nutritional profile there would probably be less opposition.

3. Germany and Scotland aren't responsible for feeding the world, besides conventional crops (not to be confused with organic) are very close to GMO crops in productivity. If your concerned with feeding the world start by ending the Ethanol mandate (which was pushed by agricultural companies) that uses 40% of the US corn crop (for reference we only use 30% for livestock) think of all the people that could feed. Finally the countries already had bans on these crops, so we really won't see any drop in production.

4. There are likely unique varieties of conventional non-GMO crops that only exist in Germany, a ban would help protect these unique varieties that may have special adaptations to the German environment, or have a unique flavor or cooking characteristics the keeps German food unique.

5. Given the demand and market growth for organic and non-GMO foods, it may be a good marketing move to have your country only grow non-GMO crops. And puts your farmers in a more profitable market (non-GMO and organic sell higher).

6. Germany and other countries may not want their farmers paying royalties to foreign companies.

7. Conventional non-gmo crops are still making productivity gains (as are GMO crops) through traditional breeding and seed chipper technology

8. Contrary to what some would have you believe, the people who make the decisions weather or not to ban GMO crops are in fact well educated on the subject of GMOs, agriculture, and the economics of agriculture. You don't get to be the head of a countries agriculture department without advance degrees and knowledge.

9. Banning a GMO isn't necessarily "anti-science" considering the companies who own the patented GMOs have full control over any study conducted (and won't allow scientific study by independent researchers, which is pretty much the definition of anti-science -- preventing someone from studying something).

And finally bans can change and be lifted if the people decide they want change.
